digest.component_or_area: code-review gate model-class wiring and LLM runner config resolution
propositions: The code-review gate silently ignores per-step model class declarations, running every LLM call on the single resolved cfg.model instead of the step's declared frontier/standard class.

The root cause is PydanticAIRunner.run discarding req.config and resolving the model from the config the runner was constructed with (cfg = self._config), so per-step model choices computed upstream never take effect.

The usage log records only op (the prompt name) and cannot attribute a call to a step, because base and the round_a/round_b batch finder share the prompt code-review-base; Step 0 adds step id and model_class (via a ContextVar) to each record.

The fix substitutes req.config.model into a copy of the runner config (_effective_config), bringing the model into line with temperature's existing per-call-override contract, without changing any code-review.yaml declaration.

An offline end-to-end test with a recording runner beneath the production RunnerAgentStep asserts each of the five steps receives its declared class and none falls through to cfg.model, and must be observed RED before the fix.

The same runner defect made four plan-review per-call model choices ineffective, including the prerequisites.py size-escalation ladder that never escalated and mis-recorded the producing model, widening the behavioural impact beyond code-review.
